title: Ops slate and exec statement (all-hands prep) v0.2
content:
Purpose and audience:
- This doc is a working sketch for the upcoming company all-hands (late March). Audience: entire company (eng, product, go-to-market, SRE, legal). Primary goals: align on near-term priorities, present draft Q2 cross-company OKRs, surface risk signals, and give a concise exec statement about platform reliability & Private readiness.

High-level narrative (executive statement draft):
- Opening line (30s): 'We shipped scale and resilience in Q1, but customers tell us predictability matters more than peak throughput. This quarter is about turning capability into dependable economics for our users.'
- Key theme 1 (45s): 'Serveability > raw model size' — emphasize latency, fallbacks, and cost controls.
- Key theme 2 (45s): Dedicated & Private readiness — progress + next steps for enterprise onboarding.
- Close (30s): call to action: 'Focus on three levers: reliability, unit cost, and rollout safety.'

Draft Q2 company-level OKRs (candidate, numerical KRs to be refined):
- O1: Make inference predictable and cheaper for Tier-1 customers
  - KR1.1: Reduce p50 end-to-end generation latency for hosted API by 12% vs baseline (baseline = Jan 2025).
  - KR1.2: Deliver 18% reduction in per-1k-token cost for common L2 workloads via batching/cache/quantization playbooks on Redwood Optimize.
  - KR1.3: Achieve 99.95% success rate for models with fallback policies under burst scenarios.

- O2: Scale Dedicated & Private to enterprise readiness
  - KR2.1: Run three pilot Private deployments (two VPC, one on-prem) with documented runbooks and customer-verified SLOs.
  - KR2.2: Ship KMS/HSM integration GA for Private customers and validate with one SOC2 client audit run.
  - KR2.3: Decrease mean time to onboard Dedicated by 30% (time from contract to traffic).

- O3: Improve developer experience for rollout and observability
  - KR3.1: Release per-route latency/cost tracing in Console for top 3 models (hosted + dedicated) and reach 60% adoption among internal beta users.
  - KR3.2: Publish 10 evaluation suites and auto-regression alerts tied to canonical prompt sets.

Notes on specificity: KRs should map to product metrics (latency dashboards, billing metrics, onboarding time). We will iterate with product leads for exact numerics.

All-hands structure (90 minutes total) — working run of show:
- 00:00–00:05 — Welcome + logistics (Asha)
- 00:05–00:15 — State of the company & exec statement (CEO) — 2 slides, 1 short customer quote
- 00:15–00:30 — Reliability & platform update (CTO + SRE lead) — recent incidents, mitigations, and SLOs
- 00:30–00:45 — Product demo: Redwood Optimize improvements and cost controls (Product)
- 00:45–00:55 — Dedicated & Private progress (Head of Sales / Head of Private) — pilots + compliance milestones
- 00:55–01:10 — Engineering showcase: serving-runtime optimizations (engineering lead) — short tech demo
- 01:10–01:25 — Q&A panel with execs (slido + live) — pre-queued + live questions
- 01:25–01:30 — Close and top asks for next 6 weeks (Asha)

Logistics and production notes:
- Location: main all-hands room (SF HQ) + Zoom + live stream to EU region. AV lead: Dylan Hart.
- Recording: yes, captions on. Post all-hands: condensed TL;DR email with timestamped highlights and edit for external partner notes.
- Rehearsals: two dry runs scheduled (week of Mar 10 and Mar 17). Expect 30–40 minute tech rehearsal for demos.
- Speaker prep: slides due Mar 3. 1-page speaker note (what to say in 90s) due Mar 7.

Q&A plan and escalation rules:
- Use Slido for pre-queued questions (collect two weeks ahead). Live questions triaged by host and SRE/product backup.
- Sensitive/legal topics: route to Legal/Privacy on-duty (Zoe Chen) before answering.

Risk register (top-of-mind pre-all-hands):
- Risk A: Recent regression in token cost model that could push up bills for top customers — mitigation: hold back any public cost claims until billing reconciliation (action: Finance + Product to sign off by Mar 5).
- Risk B: Dedicated onboarding delays due to third-party infra configs — mitigation: fallbacks in SLA language + temp credits for pilots (action: Solutions eng to draft customer comms).
- Risk C: Demo flakiness (runtime binary mismatch) — mitigation: pre-record live demo and have canned video fallback.

Communications timeline (internal & external):
- Mar 3: Final slides lock (internal).
- Mar 6: Pre-brief with customer success and sales for key accounts (who to notify if we announce new Dedicated pilots).
- Mar 12: Internal rehearsal 1 — gather pre-queued Slido questions.
- Mar 17: Full dress rehearsal with execs + AV.
- Mar 20: All-hands live. Post: TL;DR email + Confluence summary + recordings uploaded.

Action items (initial owners and due dates):
- A1: Draft final exec statement + 2 slide deck for CEO (owner: Asha) — due Mar 3.
- A2: Pull latency baseline dashboards and compute KR deltas (owner: SRE lead, Marco) — due Feb 28.
- A3: Billing validation for cost claims (owner: Finance, Priya) — due Mar 5.
- A4: Customer pilot comms and legal review (owner: Solutions eng, Zoe) — due Mar 10.
- A5: Create rehearsal checklist and pre-record demo (owner: Dylan) — due Mar 15.

Outstanding questions for leadership sync:
- Q1: Are the proposed KR targets (12% latency / 18% cost) aggressive enough to move teams but realistic given current roadmap?
- Q2: Which enterprise customers should be invited to pilot Private (we have three candidates; legal vs compliance constraints)?
- Q3: Do we want to surface any pricing changes publicly in the all-hands, or keep messaging focused on reliability & pilot availability?

Style & tone guidance for slides and speaking:
- Keep slides minimal: 3–5 bullets per slide, one visual metric per slide.
- Use customer stories to anchor technical improvements (short quote + impact statement).
- Avoid deep technical detail in exec narrative; surface it during engineering showcase and follow-up docs.

Links and references (working):
- Product roadmap page: CONFLUENCE-PRD-2401
- Incident timeline and postmortems: CONFLUENCE-INCIDENTS-2025Q1
- Billing reconciliation ticket: JIRA-OPS-341

Notes to self / loose ideas (informal):
- Consider micro-survey after all-hands to measure clarity (3 Qs: did you understand priorities? do you know your team asks? confidence in reliability?).
- Think about a short customer video (30s) showing 'before vs after' latency improvements — high impact.
- If Dedicated pilot is delayed, have fallback messaging that emphasizes roadmap and upcoming compliance milestones rather than a date.

Revision history:
- v0.1 created 2025-02-12 by Asha (initial structure and KR seeds)
- v0.2 updated 2025-02-18 by Asha (added run of show, risks, action owners, rehearsal schedule)

Please add edits directly in this doc — mark small changes with initials and date (e.g., "AK 2025-02-18: tightened KR wording").
